paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: anything you build, buy or polish up to trust in will let you down, and only the LORD is worth that trust. In Jeremiah 10:5 the LORD says idols are "Like scarecrows in a cucumber patch," and that they "can do no harm, and neither can they do any good." Then the passage says the LORD "is the true God; He is the living God and eternal King" (Jeremiah 10:10). One of them needs nails to stand up, and the other one runs the thunder. That is not a close race, friend!

Now, you might say, "Papa, I don't have a gold statue in my living room." Me neither, baker, I barely have a living room. But the idea reaches further than statues. Anything we lean on to keep us safe, to tell us what to do or to make us feel secure is a candidate. The passage warns, "Do not learn the ways of the nations or be terrified by the signs in the heavens" (Jeremiah 10:2). So we ask ourselves who is really running our fears and our hopes.

The good news is that you get to trust the One who is not a fraud. Jeremiah 10:12 says, "The LORD made the earth by His power; He established the world by His wisdom and stretched out the heavens by His understanding." And verse 16 calls Him "the Portion of Jacob," the Maker of all things, who holds Israel as His inheritance. So when something shiny starts asking for your trust, remember who made the gold, the craftsman AND the forest. Put your weight on Him, because He will never tip over.
